subject: OpenEd Collective — short-term research credit & escrow question
messages:
From: Dr. Lina Morales <lina@opened-collective.org>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: research@opened-collective.org, ada.kim@opened-collective.org
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OpenEd Collective — request for a short bridging credit and escrow flow question

Hi Olga,

Hope you’re well — I’m Lina, PI for the OpenEd Collective research network. We run a distributed student-data labeling project across five universities and are evaluating Redwood for a two-month pilot (NLP annotation + small model fine-tuning).

We have an internal grant that covers compute but the disbursement schedule is slow; before the funds arrive we’d like to request a short bridging allocation of free credits to run an initial 2–3 week burst (approx. 120k tokens). In addition to the trial credit, our procurement team is asking whether Redwood supports an escrow-style hold or usage cap (so we can guarantee we won’t exceed the provisional allocation while we finalize a formal PO).

Can you share what you can offer for academic collectives like ours (typical asks: trial top-ups, temporary spend caps, and simple one-page promo agreements)? If helpful I can attach a short project summary and expected token profile.

Thanks — we’re trying to kick this off by mid-May and would love a speedy path.

Best,
Dr. Lina Morales
Principal Investigator, OpenEd Collective
Lina.morales@opened-collective.org
+1 (415) 555-0192

--
Attachment: project-one-pager.pdf (stub)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OpenEd Collective — request for a short bridging credit and escrow flow question

Hi Lina — great to meet you over email and thanks for the clear ask.

Short answers up front: yes, we typically provide short bridging credits for academic/nonprofit pilots (amounts vary by scope), and we can implement a hard usage cap on the account while the PO is processed. We also have a one-page promotional agreement that covers the credit terms for pilots.

To propose the right amount and terms I have two quick asks: (1) can you confirm the token breakdown (ingest vs. generation) and expected peak concurrency? (2) who in procurement should I coordinate with on the billing/escrow mechanism (email/name)?

If you’re comfortable I can draft a small promo agreement and request approval from my manager for a 150k-token bridging grant and a per-account hard cap. Copying Ben and Marissa to fast-track approvals.

If useful I can also provision an isolated sandbox project in our Dedicated demo pool to limit blast radius.

— Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Ben / Marissa — forwarding a new academic pilot request. Key details: multi-university nonprofit, ~120k tokens initial ask, wants a hard spend cap/escrow while PO clears. Tentative kickoff mid-May.

My recommendation: approve a 150k-token bridging credit and set account hard cap to 150k tokens for the sandbox project. Include a one-page promo agreement (low legal risk, standard terms) and require the PO for additional funds beyond the cap. I’ll own the procurement coordination.

Rationale: high likelihood of conversion to paid pilot; low risk due to per-account cap and short time window. Approvals needed for credit amount and signature on the promo agreement.

If you prefer smaller amount, 100k still gives them ability to validate.

— Olga

Hi Lina — thanks for reaching out and for the project summary (helpful). Happy to approve the pilot support.

What we’re offering:
- 150,000 trial tokens credited to an isolated sandbox project (valid for 35 days from issuance)
- A hard usage cap (150k tokens) will be configured on the account to prevent overage while the PO is in flight
- We’ll send a one-page promo agreement outlining the credit & cap; signature by a procurement contact will be required to release additional funds

Attachments: promo-agreement.pdf (one-page), usage-estimate.xlsx (token breakdown template). I’ve also uploaded the promo agreement to our shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/s/abc123-promo-agreement

Next steps for Lina / OpenEd Collective:
1) Confirm the sandbox project name you’d like created and provide a procurer contact (name + email) for the promo agreement signature
2) If you can, provide a quick ingest/generation token split (ballpark is fine) so we can tune the sandbox to expected concurrency

Olga — I’ve approved and attached the one-pager. Please proceed to create the sandbox and set the cap; loop me in on the DocuSign if they need signature.

Best,
